text: In nineteen twenty-four, the way up Angels Landing had no chains and no Walter's Wiggles.
A newspaper described the ridge beyond Scout Lookout as narrowing from ten feet to ten inches.
The trail cut into solid rock came in nineteen twenty-six. The chains were added decades later.
Walter's Wiggles is a run of twenty-one steep switchbacks, cut into solid rock in nineteen twenty-six.
It is named for Walter Ruesch, the first superintendent of Zion National Park.
It is the last hurdle before Scout Lookout, on the way up Angels Landing.
The Narrows from the top down is sixteen miles, one way, starting outside the park.
The walls rise up to a thousand feet. In places, the gorge is only thirty feet wide.
The park says at least eighty percent of the route is wading, walking and swimming.
The Angels Landing climb is five point four miles round trip, with a fourteen hundred eighty-eight foot climb.
A pastor from Ogden named it in nineteen sixteen. Before that, it was known as the Temple of Aeolus.
The top-down Narrows takes an estimated ten to fourteen hours, or two days with an overnight permit.
The park closes it when the river runs above one hundred twenty cubic feet per second, and during flash flood warnings.
